sources: ERIC ED208681, 'English pronunciation problems of Vietnamese speakers' (final consonants, clusters)
ICHUSO 2019 paper 034, error taxonomy: deletion, epenthesis, devoicing, omission+epenthesis

sounds.label: -ed said as /t/ after a voiceless sound
sounds.why_l1: Vietnamese syllables end in a few unreleased consonants and never in a cluster, so the /t/ added by -ed after /k p s ʃ tʃ f/ is easy to drop.
sounds.tip_en: Hold the last sound, then release a short, crisp T: walk-T.
sounds.tip_l1: Giữ âm cuối rồi bật nhẹ một âm T ngắn: walk-T. Đừng nuốt mất âm T.
sounds.speech_hint: the T sound at the end

sentences: She walked to the shops yesterday.
We looked everywhere and asked for help.

sounds.label: -ed said as /d/ after a voiced sound
sounds.why_l1: A voiced /d/ never ends a Vietnamese syllable, so it is dropped or devoiced to an unreleased /t/.
sounds.tip_en: Keep your voice on through the final D: move-D.
sounds.tip_l1: Giữ rung dây thanh đến hết âm D cuối: move-D.
sounds.speech_hint: the D sound at the end

sentences: They moved here and played football all summer.

sounds.label: Plural and third-person -s
sounds.why_l1: Vietnamese marks plural and person with separate words, not endings, so the final -s/-z carries no meaning for the ear and gets dropped.
sounds.tip_en: Finish the word with a clear hiss: book-S, need-Z.
sounds.tip_l1: Kết thúc từ bằng một tiếng xì rõ: book-S, need-Z.
sounds.speech_hint: the S sound at the end

sentences: She needs two books and works on weekends.

sounds.label: Voiceless TH /θ/
sounds.why_l1: Vietnamese has no /θ/; the closest sounds are /t/ (written th in Vietnamese, aspirated) and /s/.
sounds.tip_en: Put your tongue tip lightly between your teeth and blow air: th-ink.
sounds.tip_l1: Đặt đầu lưỡi nhẹ giữa hai hàm răng rồi thổi hơi ra: th-ink. Không phải 'th' tiếng Việt.

sentences: I think three months is enough.

sounds.label: Voiced TH /ð/
sounds.why_l1: Vietnamese has no /ð/; learners substitute /d/ or /z/.
sounds.tip_en: Same tongue position as think, but turn your voice on: the, this.
sounds.tip_l1: Lưỡi đặt giống như 'think' nhưng rung dây thanh: the, this.

sentences: They said this weather is better than the other day.

sounds.label: Final consonant clusters
sounds.why_l1: Vietnamese syllables never end in two consonants, so learners keep one and drop the rest.
sounds.tip_en: Say every consonant at the end, slowly at first: mo-s-t.
sounds.tip_l1: Đọc đủ từng phụ âm cuối, lúc đầu chậm: mo-s-t.

sentences: Most students passed the first test.

sounds.label: Starting consonant clusters
sounds.why_l1: Vietnamese syllables start with one consonant, so learners insert a vowel inside clusters (s-treet) or drop one consonant.
sounds.tip_en: Glide straight from S into the next sound, no vowel in between: street.
sounds.tip_l1: Lướt thẳng từ S sang âm sau, không chêm nguyên âm: street, không phải 'sơ-trít'.

sentences: The students play sport in the street every spring.

sounds.label: Final stop consonants /p t k b d g/
sounds.why_l1: Vietnamese final stops are unreleased, so English final stops are often not heard at all.
sounds.tip_en: Release the last consonant with a small puff of air: wee-K.
sounds.tip_l1: Bật nhẹ phụ âm cuối với một luồng hơi nhỏ: wee-K.

sentences: Next week I need a big bag for my job.

sounds.label: Final L
sounds.why_l1: Vietnamese has no syllable-final /l/; learners drop it or turn it into a vowel or /n/.
sounds.tip_en: Touch the tongue tip to the ridge behind your top teeth at the end: hal-L.
sounds.tip_l1: Cuối từ chạm đầu lưỡi lên lợi sau răng trên: hal-L.
sounds.speech_hint: the L sound at the end

sentences: I feel careful in the school hall.

sounds.label: SH /ʃ/ versus S /s/
sounds.why_l1: Many Vietnamese speakers (especially southern) merge s and x, so English /ʃ/ and /s/ blur together.
sounds.tip_en: Round your lips and pull the tongue back a little for SH: she, not see.
sounds.tip_l1: Tròn môi và kéo lưỡi lùi vào một chút cho âm SH: she, không phải see.

sentences: She went shopping at the station.

sounds.label: Z /z/ said as S
sounds.why_l1: Southern Vietnamese has no /z/ (d and gi are said as /j/), so /z/ is devoiced to /s/.
sounds.tip_en: Make it buzz: put a hand on your throat and feel it vibrate on Z.
sounds.tip_l1: Làm cho nó rung: đặt tay lên cổ họng, cảm thấy rung khi nói Z.

sentences: It is easy to win a prize at the zoo.

sounds.label: Initial P /p/
sounds.why_l1: Native Vietnamese words do not start with /p/ (it appears mostly in loanwords), so learners voice it to /b/.
sounds.tip_en: Build up air behind your lips and pop it out: P-en. Hold paper in front of your mouth; it should move.
sounds.tip_l1: Dồn hơi sau hai môi rồi bật ra: P-en. Để tờ giấy trước miệng, tờ giấy phải rung.
sounds.speech_hint: the P sound at the start

sentences: People pay a fair price for paper in the park.
